settings.headline: Your snoring keeps you both awake.
settings.lead_before: Snoring is the sound of your mouth doing your nose's job. In a controlled trial of congested snorers, a nasal dilator cut snoring frequency by about
settings.lead_after: against a dummy strip. The band holds that same airway open, all night.
settings.citation: Pevernagie, D., Hamans, E., Van Cauwenberge, P., Pauwels, R. (2000). External nasal dilation reduces snoring in chronic rhinitis patients: a randomized controlled trial. European Respiratory Journal, 15(6), 996-1000.
settings.fig_caption: Snoring frequency, dummy strip versus nasal dilator, schematic.
settings.toc_title: Snoring and the person beside you

settings.headline: Opening the narrowest part changes everything.
settings.lead_before: One nostril always feels blocked. Widen the nasal valve and the effort of breathing through your nose drops. In a congested nose, a dilator strip cut nasal resistance by about
settings.lead_after: . That is the whole job of the band.
settings.citation: Gehring, J.M., Garlick, S.R., Wheatley, J.R., Amis, T.C. (2000). Nasal resistance and flow resistive work of nasal breathing during exercise: effects of a nasal dilator strip. Journal of Applied Physiology, 89(3), 1114-1122.
settings.fig_caption: Nasal resistance in a congested nose, with and without a dilator strip, schematic.

settings.headline: A blocked nose is a half-finished night.
settings.lead_before: You do not have to wake up to lose sleep. In a four-week randomised trial, people using a nasal dilator strip reported better sleep and less daytime impairment than the control group. Clear the nose and you cut the quiet interruptions you never feel.
settings.citation: Krakow, B., Melendrez, D., Sisley, B., et al. (2006). Nasal dilator strip therapy for chronic sleep-maintenance insomnia and symptoms of sleep-disordered breathing: a randomized controlled trial. Sleep and Breathing, 10(1), 16-28.
settings.fig_caption: Reported sleep quality across four weeks of nightly strip use, schematic.

settings.headline: Bad sleep doesn't follow a bad mood. It leads it.
settings.lead_before: Sleep and mood run on the same wire. Pooling years of long-term studies, people with insomnia were around
settings.lead_after: as likely to become depressed over time. The band won't fix your mood. Steadier sleep is just where a steadier day starts.
settings.citation: Baglioni, C., Battagliese, G., Feige, B., et al. (2011). Insomnia as a predictor of depression: a meta-analytic evaluation of longitudinal epidemiological studies. Journal of Affective Disorders, 135(1-3), 10-19.
settings.fig_caption: Relative risk of later depression by sleep quality, schematic.

settings.headline: Your nose is built for the work. Your mouth is the backup.
settings.lead_before: Push hard and you bail to mouth breathing, and you skip the work your nose was doing. It warms air toward body temperature, around
settings.lead_after: deeper in the nose, and nearly saturates it with moisture before it reaches your lungs. The band keeps that nasal route the easy option when you train.
settings.citation: Lindemann, J., Keck, T., Wiesmiller, K., et al. (2002). Nasal mucosal temperature during respiration. Clinical Otolaryngology and Allied Sciences, 27(3), 135-139.
settings.fig_caption: Air conditioning the nose performs on each inhaled breath, schematic.

settings.headline: Morning breath is a dry-mouth problem.
settings.lead_before: Sleep with your mouth open and it dries out by morning, and saliva is your overnight defence. In adults, inflamed gums healed at just
settings.lead_after: of mouth breathers' dried-out sites, against 69% of everyone else. Breathe through your nose and your mouth stays closed and moist.
settings.citation: Mehta, S., et al. (2018). Influence of mouth breathing on the outcome of scaling and root planing in chronic periodontitis. BDJ Open, 4, 17039.
settings.fig_caption: Gum healing at dried-out sites after the same treatment, schematic.

settings.headline: Your nose makes something your mouth can't.
settings.lead_before: Breathe through your nose and your sinuses release nitric oxide, a gas that helps widen blood vessels and that the mouth route skips entirely. Slow, gentle nasal breathing raised it many times over, up to
settings.lead_after: when humming. The band doesn't make nitric oxide. Your nose does. It just keeps that route open.
settings.citation: Weitzberg, E., Lundberg, J.O.N. (2002). Humming greatly increases nasal nitric oxide. American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine, 166(2), 144-145.
settings.fig_caption: Nasal nitric oxide, quiet breathing versus humming, schematic.

settings.headline: Short sleep leaves the door open.
settings.lead_before: The nights you cut sleep short are the nights you catch what is going around. When healthy people were exposed to a live cold virus, those sleeping under five hours were about
settings.lead_after: as likely to fall ill. No strip fights a virus. But easier breathing helps you sleep, and better sleep is one thing you can do something about.
settings.citation: Prather, A.A., Janicki-Deverts, D., Hall, M.H., Cohen, S. (2015). Behaviorally assessed sleep and susceptibility to the common cold. Sleep, 38(9), 1353-1359.
settings.fig_caption: Odds of catching a cold after exposure, by sleep duration, schematic.

settings.cover_subtitle: The benefits of our nasal strip
settings.toc_field: In the order you feel it
settings.closing_headline: The band holds your nose open. The rest follows.
settings.closing_lead: The research is clear, using the aira strip will provide you with many benefits, from reduced snoring to increased sporting performance. We believe it will be a benefit to everyone, in one way or another. That is why we offer a 30-night guarantee.
settings.ship_line: Free shipping in the UAE. 30-night guarantee.
settings.small_print: The aira band opens your nasal airway mechanically. It is not a treatment for snoring, sleep apnoea, chronic congestion, or a structural problem, and it does not replace medical care. If you think you have any of those, see your doctor. Figures on these pages are schematic representations of reported results.
